construction: Use sya in the ordinary future and conditional, tās in luṭ, and sīyuṭ in the benedictive. 6.4.62 gives an optional ciṇ-like operation on the preceding aṅga together with iṭ on the actual outer affix. The latter remains sya/tās/sīyuṭ, and 6.4.104 deletion of ta belongs to actual ciṇ. Consonant-final lexical inputs outside the named group do not freely acquire this option.
policies: Two styai roots are vowel-final in teaching. Ordinary aniṭ ā leads to styāsyate, and ciṇvat yuk with iṭ yields styāyiṣyate. They share these third-singular activity pairs; their other persons would require a different construction.
In the three lexical ṇic profiles ordinary ay remains before outer iṭ, and ciṇvat gives the selected bare radical factor after lopa. The ordinary and ciṇvat forms both enter each licensed case.

For basic nam the active sak rule of 7.2.73 concerns sic and P. These nonagentive future/benedictive requests have independent ordinary aniṭ words. Before t the earlier m has the dental realization in nantā; before s the result is naṃsyate/naṃsīṣṭa.
In the curādi mah benedictive 2pl, the ciṇvat factor ends in h before iṭ, allowing both dh and ḍh on the inherited interpretation. The archive records the retroflex spelling only on that branch.
